tasks.extracted: Of 23,470 records, 328 studies were retained, with general-population data from 50 countries in all six WHO regions. Prevalence was pooled by country-specific random-effects meta-analysis for 29 countries and predicted for 158 countries with one or no study (or a pooled interval of 0 to 100%) by fractional response regression on GDP per capita at purchasing power parity, women's mean total alcohol consumption and WHO region (Europe split into EU and non-EU states, the Americas into Canada and the USA against the rest); the predictions were made for the year 2012. Editors' arithmetic: 21 of the 50 countries with data (50 minus 29) were given predicted values in place of their observed ones.

tasks.extracted: Of 11,110 records, 62 FAS studies were retained, with data from 19 countries in four WHO regions (African, Americas, European, Western Pacific): 22 used active case ascertainment, 20 passive surveillance, 14 were clinic-based and 6 used mixed methods, and 40 used an established diagnostic guideline or stated their case definition. FAS was pooled by meta-analysis for 7 countries (primary analysis: active case ascertainment or clinic-based studies with a stated guideline or case definition) and, for 180 countries, computed by applying a quotient of women who drank in pregnancy per FAS case to the country's drinking prevalence. The five highest country estimates per 10,000: Belarus 69.1 (42.1–103.5; predicted), Italy 82.1 (42.1–134.6), Ireland 89.7 (50.4–142.8; predicted), Croatia 115.2 (34.8–236.0) and South Africa 585.3 (430.7–761.7).
